newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuanian shares edge up in more active market.
newsitem.headline: Lithuanian shares edge up in more active market.

text.p: Lithuanian shares edged up on Thursday and the market showed signs of increased activity after a protracted slump, dealers said.
The group A index climbed 32.35 points to 2,444.29 on turnover of 1.84 million litas.
"Prices are good and some buyers are coming back to the market," Aidas Galubickas of brokerage Suprema told Reuters.
Energy sector shares were relatively in demand and extended their recent gains sparked by the government's pledge to reform and privatise the sector.
Lithuania Energy shares turned over 425,000 litas and its price adavanced to 3.11 litas from 3.00 litas.
Lithuanian Gas rose to 2.15 litas from 2.11 in trade of 191,600 litas.
Maziekiu Nafta also gained, rising to 10.57 litas from 10.31 in trade of 24,300 litas.
Losers included Birzai Milk, which fell to 10 litas from 10.20 in trade worth 100,300 litas.
The bank sector was mixed in anticipation of the release of 1996 results, which dealers say will have a big impact.
Hermis Bank, Snoras Bank and Litimpeks lost ground. Hermis fell to 175.50 litas from 189.90 litas in trade of 47,600 litas after falling ten percent on Wednesday.
Snoras Bank slipped to 28.00 litas from 30.00 and 14,000 litas worth of shares changed hands while Litimpeks dropped to 6.51 litas from 7.02 in trade of 4,465 litas.
The secondary T-bill market was relatively active in trade of over 3.9 million litas.
